prompt.context: American Beauty Company (ABC) is, as the name suggests, a high quality beauty products company. They have done very well both in the US and globally and enjoy great brand recognition. One of their major products is hair color. ABC manufactures high quality 'use at home' hair color products. They sell through retail and drugstores, with all manufacturing in-house. They have an 800 number for customer support. Recently they have been experiencing declining revenues and market shares. The retailers have complained about their products as the competition Bell International takes over. The firm has been called in to advise ABC on what to do.
prompt.question: How would you start thinking about this problem?

clarifying_info.q: What segments make up the hair color market?
clarifying_info.a: The main segments are Women (18-55), Men, and Teens.

clarifying_info.q: Do we have data on market size and growth rates by segment?
clarifying_info.a: Yes — Women: $800M today, growing 5% per year; Men: $200M today, growing 20% per year; Teens: $100M today, growing 10% per year.

clarifying_info.q: What is ABC's current market share by segment?

clarifying_info.a: Bell International is the primary competitor taking share from ABC.

exhibits.title: Customer Brand Awareness and Perception Survey (18-55 Women Segment)
exhibits.shows: A survey table benchmarking ABC against competitor Bell International on brand awareness and perception of quality among users and non-users in the 18-55 women segment
exhibits.data: Rows: ABC and Bell; Columns include brand awareness and perception of quality metrics broken out by users and non-users

framework: Product: attributes, ease of use, value proposition, price, benchmark against competitors, market share and trends
Customer: target market segments, brand loyalty, price sensitivity, important attributes, typical customer behavior, purchasing habits
Distribution Channel: distribution network breadth, shelf space and positioning, share of distribution network compared to competitors

questions.prompt: One of ABC's biggest market segments is 18-55 year old women, but their share has been declining recently. Why might this be happening and how would you approach this issue?
questions.guidance: Break the problem into two parts: (1) Diagnose why share is declining — lack of brand awareness, low trial rate among this segment, low re-trial/re-purchase rate suggesting quality issues, or access/distribution problems. (2) Explain how to test each hypothesis — use marketing research to identify which factor ABC is lacking, and compare results against industry and competitor benchmarks.

questions.prompt: Using the market data provided, what sales are required for ABC to have 50% of the women's market in 2 years?
questions.guidance: Candidate should project the women's segment size in 2 years using the 5% annual growth rate, then calculate 50% of that figure. Women's market in 2 years = $800M * (1.05)^2 = $882M; 50% of that = $441M. Current ABC women's revenue = $800M * 0.50 = $400M. So ABC needs to grow women's revenue from $400M to $441M — an increase of $41M.

math.setup: Women's market today = $800M, growing at 5%/yr. Target = 50% share in 2 years.
math.answer: ABC needs $441M in women's segment sales in 2 years, which is $41M more than its current $400M.

questions.prompt: What is ABC's current dollar market share? What will it be in 2 years (assuming same share percentages)?
questions.guidance: Sum ABC's revenue across all three segments at current market sizes and shares. Then project total market sizes two years out using respective growth rates, apply same share percentages, and compute new total and share percentage. Note that ABC's percentage share declines because the men's segment (where ABC has only 10% share) is growing fastest at 20%/yr.

math.setup: Current market: Women $800M (50% ABC), Men $200M (10% ABC), Teens $100M (30% ABC). Growth: Women 5%/yr, Men 20%/yr, Teens 10%/yr.
math.answer: Current ABC dollar market share = $450M (~41%). In 2 years = ~$506M (~39.2%). Share % declines because ABC has very low penetration in the fast-growing men's segment.

questions.prompt: The team conducted a customer brand awareness and perception survey in the 18-55 women segment benchmarking ABC against Bell. What do you notice and what do you suggest ABC do about it? (Exhibit 1)
questions.guidance: Despite ABC's high quality and strong brand recognition, Bell fares better among both users and non-users on both brand awareness and perception of quality. ABC should: (1) Invest in advertising to improve brand awareness; (2) Invest in promotions, trials, and joint marketing efforts with retailers to improve perception of quality and drive trial.

questions.prompt: Please summarize your findings and give a recommendation to the ABC CEO.
questions.guidance: Structured conclusion covering: (1) Main finding — competitor Bell has achieved superior brand awareness and perception of quality vs. ABC, driving revenue and share decline; (2) Recommendations — invest in advertising to close the awareness gap, run aggressive promotions and joint retailer marketing to improve quality perception and drive trials; (3) Growth opportunities — ABC has very low men's segment penetration (10%) while that segment is growing 20%/yr; target men for future growth. Teen segment is small but could expand via innovative products and increased acceptance. Note women's segment is maturing.

brainstorming.prompt: Why might ABC's market share in the 18-55 women segment be declining?

categories.name: Brand Awareness
ideas: Lack of brand awareness vs. Bell

categories.name: Trial & Purchase
ideas: Low trial rate — consumers have not tried ABC products
Low re-trial/re-purchase rate suggesting quality or experience issues
Consumers defaulting to Bell due to better promotions

categories.name: Product
ideas: Limited shade range or ease-of-use issues
Price premium not justified in consumers' minds

categories.name: Distribution
ideas: Less shelf space or worse shelf positioning vs. Bell
Retailers preferring Bell due to better margins or support
Weaker presence in certain channel types (e.g., online)

categories.name: Competitive Actions
ideas: Bell running aggressive promotions targeting ABC's core segment
Bell investing more in joint retailer marketing
Bell improving product quality or launching new variants

recommendation: ABC's declining revenue and market share is primarily driven by Bell International achieving superior brand awareness and perception of quality among the core 18-55 women segment, despite ABC's objectively high-quality products

ABC should immediately invest in advertising to close the brand awareness gap with Bell, and run aggressive in-store promotions, trials, and joint retailer marketing campaigns to improve quality perception and convert non-users
risks: Advertising and promotional investment may compress margins before revenue recovers
Women's segment is maturing (5% growth), limiting upside even with improved share
Men's segment penetration strategy requires new marketing capabilities and potentially product adjustments
next_steps: Launch targeted advertising campaign to boost brand awareness in the 18-55 women segment and benchmark awareness metrics quarterly against Bell
Develop joint marketing and trial promotion programs with key retail and drugstore partners
Develop a dedicated go-to-market strategy for the men's segment given its 20%/yr growth rate and ABC's current 10% share
Explore product and marketing innovation in the teen segment to expand total addressable market
